surprises.description: Repligen’s adjusted EPS was $0.53, well above the preview’s $0.4628 consensus estimate. The roughly 15% beat was larger than the preview’s deliberately low EPS bar suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose 15% to $0.53 from $0.46 a year earlier.”

surprises.description: Capital equipment orders grew at a mid-teens rate and reached their highest level in five years, stronger than the preview’s expectation of another book-to-bill-above-1 quarter and continued improvement. However, most system deliveries were pushed into 2027, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the order pickup would convert later.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Capital equipment orders grew mid-teens year-over-year to the highest orders quarter in five years, but revenue declined as most system deliveries were pushed by customers into 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A second consecutive >1.0 quarter plus the third RFP is the single most important disclosure on the call.”

surprises.description: Repligen’s adjusted operating margin was 15.9%, above the preview’s quarterly estimate of 15.0–15.3%. That is a better margin result than the preview’s EPS build assumed, even though it remains within the company’s existing full-year margin guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin expanded 170 basis points year-over-year to 15.9%.”

surprises.description: Filtration fell 11% in the quarter, and management now expects the franchise to be flat to slightly down for the full year rather than meeting the preview’s mid-single-digit growth expectation. The decline included the polymer divestiture and FX, but was still materially weaker than that forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Filtration revenue fell 11% (including a 2-point polymer divestiture and FX headwind), and full-year filtration is now expected to be flat to slightly down.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “filtration mid-single-digit” for the FY target set at Q2.

surprises.description: The BioLife contribution included in 2026 guidance is about $24 million, below the preview’s arithmetic estimate of a roughly $29–30 million Q4 stub. That makes the expected partial-year revenue contribution smaller than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was raised ... including a ~$24 million partial-quarter BioLife contribution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “BioLife did $28.5M in Q2, +21% y/y, so a ~$29–30M stub is the arithmetic.”

surprises.description: The quarter included a $41 million non-cash impairment tied to an old IP license agreement, an unanticipated charge in GAAP results. It was excluded from adjusted figures, so it did not account for the adjusted EPS beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP results included a $41 million non-cash intangible impairment from an old IP license agreement, excluded from adjusted figures.”

surprises.description: Chromatography grew more than 50% in the quarter, and its full-year growth outlook is now at least 30%, above the preview’s expectation of more than 20%. This is a stronger franchise result and outlook than the preview’s baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Chromatography grew over 50% ... in the quarter, with full-year guidance of at least 30% for chromatography and analytics.”

surprises.description: Management’s full-year analytics growth outlook of at least 30% is above the preview’s expected threshold of at least 25%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year guidance of at least 30% for chromatography and analytics.”

surprises.description: Management set a 2027 growth floor of at least 25%, which implies revenue above $1 billion but is below the preview’s 29.1% growth consensus and $1.08 billion estimate if growth lands near that floor. The wording is a minimum, not a firm ceiling or point forecast, so the gap is not definitive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided to at least 25% reported top-line growth in 2027, pushing revenue above $1 billion.”

surprises.description: Asia Pacific revenue declined slightly despite the preview’s focus on regional durability after strong Q2 growth. China remained strong, but the broader region did not sustain that prior growth rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China revenue grew over 40% in the quarter and over 50% year-to-date, while overall Asia Pacific revenue declined slightly against a record prior-year comparison.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “China / APAC durability and customer mix. APAC +40% in Q2, China +60% in H1.”

surprises.description: Quarterly revenue of $209 million beat the $206.71 million consensus estimate, although it landed within the preview’s expected sequential revenue range of roughly $206–210 million. The consensus beat was therefore modest rather than a clear break from the preview’s operating scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q3 2026 revenue of $209 million, up 11% reported and 12.5% organic.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $206.71M”; the preview also framed Q3 as “$206–210M.”
